$comment: ADR-0008's normative rules: what one Fathom commit row's numbers mean.
This file is the machine-readable form of docs/adr/0008-per-commit-metric-model.md. It is the ONE
spelling of the selection pipeline, the drop-reason vocabulary, the aggregation arithmetic, the
action-success state machine and the glyph table. scripts/metric_model_reference.py loads it and is
the oracle mact-by1.6's Rust reader is graded against, and the ADR's fenced blocks are diffed
against it by scripts/validate_metric_model.py. Prose that disagrees with this file is a bug in the
Changing anything here changes the meaning of every row already in every .fathom cache: bump the
evidence-derivation analyzer version (ADR-0006 section 6.3) in the same commit, and if the change
alters a row field's meaning rather than adding a field, bump `row_version` (ADR-0006 section 6.4).
The evidence contract itself does not change here: ADR-0002 stays normative about records, this
file is normative about what a reader derives from them.

consumes.reader: crates/act-evidence (ADR-0005): the record types, never a second struct set
consumes.store: ADR-0006 section 6.4 rows: coverage, benchmarks, action_success, gaps
consumes.renderer: mact-by1.9 timeline, mact-by1.12 bench panel, mact-by1.13 report and doctor

row_key.rule: a directory name under .evidence is always 40 lowercase hex (ADR-0002 section 1.1), so a short-SHA path join is a bug, not a shortcut

stage_meaning.walk: which bytes are read at all
stage_meaning.retain: which records a number may be built from, per record, in path order
stage_meaning.select: which retained run is the newest for its identity
stage_meaning.aggregate: the arithmetic that turns the selected records into the row's numbers

pipeline.explain_rule: every record read is either retained or dropped with exactly one reason code from drop_reasons; --explain and gaps exist so a wrong number is answerable (mact-by1.6)

walk.rule: kind/<full-sha>/<run_id>.jsonl and nothing else; a glob of ** / *.jsonl walks into runs/<run_id>/act.jsonl, which is act's log and not a record

retention.other_statuses_are: written on purpose (ADR-0002 section 4.4) so a broken run is visible and filterable; they never feed a number and are always listed in the row
retention.measure_rule: one measure per pooled number; records of a non-primary measure are never pooled with it because istanbul statements are a different unit from lcov lines (ADR-0002 section 4.2)
retention.benchmark_precedence_rule: within one run and one group, the highest-precedence source present wins and the others are dropped as source_shadowed; this is ADR-0002 section 5.1's precedence applied to what survived the writer's own dedup

drop_reasons.meaning: dot-file: .<run_id>.jsonl.<random>.tmp is a crashed publish (ADR-0002 section 1.1)
directory name is not 40 lowercase hex: short SHA, mixed case, or a foreign name
schema_version newer than this build reads: skip and count, never guess (ADR-0002 section 7; the same rule ADR-0007 checker follows)
not strict JSON, not one object, missing a required envelope field, a kind disagreeing with its directory, a last byte that is not LF (a torn write), or a schema failure
the record's commit is not the directory it was read from; the directory is trusted, the record is dropped (ADR-0002 section 1.1)
run_id does not match ADR-0002 section 1.2, so it cannot be sorted and cannot be selected
flags contains truncated: the run hit the metric cap, so what survived must never be summed and called the run (ADR-0002 section 5.1)
excluded by fathom.toml benchmarks.allow / benchmarks.deny (ADR-0006 section 7.2)
same run, same group, lower-precedence source (retention.benchmark_precedence_within_run)
an older run of the same (kind, workflow, task) group: kept for spread and for --explain, never part of the headline value
reported_percent with no raw counts: a caveat, never a plotted number (ADR-0002 section 4.3)
flags contains low_confidence: text-scraped, a caveat, never a plotted number
found == 0: the ratio is undefined, the entry contributes nothing to a pool and is excluded from any average (ADR-0002 section 4.3)
the record's measure is not the commit's primary measure: kept as a secondary number, never pooled with it
coverage record with no complete count pair: nothing to pool
a file record of a run that also published a total: the run's own total is that run's number (ADR-0002 section 4.3)

selection.newest_rule: lexical maximum of run_id, which is the chronologically newest run because the id embeds a UTC timestamp (ADR-0002 section 1.2)
selection.ties: impossible: run_id is unique per run and one file is exactly one run
selection.per_kind_because: one run may publish one file per kind; grouping without kind would let a benchmark run supersede a coverage run
selection.git_log_order_note: git log yields newest-first and ls yields oldest-first; the rule is a max over the group, so neither order can get it wrong

row_shape.$comment: the closed field list the derivation emits, as a supplement to ADR-0006 section 6.4's row: coverage, benchmarks, action_success and gaps are that row's fields, extended here with the detail this ADR owns. A reader may assume nothing else is present; a writer may not add a field without adding it here, to the ADR and to the golden vectors in the same commit.
row_shape.gaps_adr0006_note: these three keys of the row's gaps object belong to ADR-0006 and ADR-0007, not here; this ADR writes only the two above, and gaps.no_evidence is true exactly when action_success is no_evidence
row_shape.nulls: none anywhere: an unknown value is an absent key (ADR-0002 2.1, ADR-0006 6.3), which is why a benchmark with no unit has no unit key at all rather than a null one

gap_reasons.$comment: a column with no number carries exactly one of these; it is what the unknown glyph stands for and what doctor and --explain print
priority: nothing readable at this SHA: unreadable if a record was present but unreadable, else no_evidence
coverage: percent_only or low_confidence was the only thing there: only_percent_only
coverage: every pooled denominator was 0: vacuous
a run at this SHA was excluded by retention: all_runs_excluded
benchmarks: a name was filtered by config: config_filtered
coverage: a record had no count pair at all: no_counts

caveat_codes.$comment: the closed set a row's caveats[] may contain; the timeline shows one marker glyph and the detail view names the codes
caveat_codes.marker_glyph: the glyph appended to a column whose value has caveats; it never appears on a column with no value behind it

coverage.identity: (commit, kind, run_id, scope, path) per ADR-0002 section 4.4
coverage.per_run_total_rule: a selected run's scope:total record IS that run's total and is used directly; only when a run has no total record are its file records summed, and then the row carries the caveat total_from_file_sum
coverage.sum_invariant_note: sum(file records) == total is FALSE by design: a tool that instrumented files outside the workspace puts them in the total and in no file record (ADR-0002 section 4.2). A reader must not treat the difference as corruption and must not renumber the total
coverage.pool: sum of numerators over sum of denominators across the selected runs, per measure
coverage.pool_flat: sum of numerators over sum of denominators, per measure
coverage.never: average per-file percentages; average per-run percentages; use a rounded intermediate as an input
coverage.primary_measure: first entry of retention.measure_order whose pooled found > 0
coverage.secondary_measures: every other measure with pooled found > 0, pooled the same way and stored under coverage.secondary
coverage.percent_input: raw counts only, never a rounded intermediate
coverage.rounding: half away from zero, from the raw counts only; the stored digit is what a renderer prints
coverage.vacuous: found == 0 after pooling: coverage is absent, reason vacuous, glyph is the unknown glyph, and the commit is excluded from any window average; a vacuous record inside a non-vacuous pool is a no-op because 0/0 adds nothing to either sum
coverage.zero_is_zero: hit == 0 with found > 0 is a real 0.0 %, rendered as a number with a down-delta, never as the unknown glyph
coverage.excluded_still_shown: as caveat markers on the row and as named entries in the detail view, with reported_percent, reported_measure and source_path
coverage.single_percent_only_commit: coverage absent + caveat percent_only: the scraped number is a signal that something ran, never this commit's coverage %
coverage.superseded_runs_kept: listed in coverage.superseded_runs so a re-run is visible
coverage.pooled_bound: pooling is a size-weighted mean of the selected runs' rates, so the pooled percent is always between the smallest and the largest of them; it can neither invent coverage nor hide a drop

benchmarks.identity: (commit, kind, run_id, name, labels, sample) per ADR-0002 section 4.4
benchmarks.sample_note: samples are the noise estimate, not duplicates; a dedup that drops them throws away the spread
benchmarks.group_key_rule: unit is part of the identity, so a metric whose unit changed is a different metric and cannot be plotted against its former self; an absent unit is its own group key (unit_missing)
benchmarks.value: median over the samples of the newest selected run
benchmarks.spread_flat: min and max over every retained run of that group
benchmarks.median_even_n: mean of the two middle values (ascending by value), which is what docs/evidence-format.md recipe 6 prints
benchmarks.median_even_n_flat: mean of the two middle values
benchmarks.median_population: all records of the group in that run, whether or not sample is set: the writer numbers samples only when a job really emitted more than one (ADR-0002 section 4.4)
benchmarks.spread: min and max over the RETAINED records of the group at this commit (every successful, non-truncated run), with runs = distinct run_id count; the spread deliberately spans superseded runs
benchmarks.spread_single_run: min == max with runs == 1 is an unmeasured noise floor, not a stable metric; a renderer says so rather than drawing a confidence interval out of one number
benchmarks.serialization: shortest round-trip decimal of the binary64 value (Rust {}, Python repr, jq 1.7.1 agree); never re-rounded for storage
benchmarks.display_precision: 4 significant digits, half away from zero, at render time only
benchmarks.comparable: unit present and identical across the group's history; unit_missing means displayable but not comparable: no delta, no sparkline, no cross-metric axis
never_compare: different metric names on one axis
act_log context rows against a job_file measurement
benchmarks.context_rule: job_duration_s and step_duration_s describe the run, not the code: kept, shown with the context glyph, and never a regression signal by default
benchmarks.absent_is_not_zero: step_duration_s is legitimately absent on act 0.2.62..0.2.75 (docs/evidence-format.md section 5); absence renders as the unknown glyph with a reason and is never a hole, a 0 or a regression
benchmarks.headline: every retained group after the fathom.toml allow/deny filter; the timeline's single bench column shows the first group in (name, canon(labels)) order plus a +N for the rest, preferring a comparable group over a context one
benchmarks.missing_group_vs_zero: a group absent at this commit is absent: no 0, no carry-forward from the parent, no interpolation across commits

action_success.durable_source: the run_status field on every evidence record (ADR-0002 section 2.2): it is in the contract, it is on disk, and it is the only thing that answers the question three weeks later
never_the_source: the run_status MCP tool: in-memory, newest 50, evicts, and answers run_not_found afterwards (docs/tool-contract.md section 5)
runs/<run_id>/meta.json in the index path: audit material, not the contract (ADR-0002 section 1.3)
the server of any kind: fathom is a reader, never a client (ADR-0005 section 7)
action_success.group_verdict: the newest run's run_status for that group (selection.newest_by), so a failed run followed by a successful re-run is a pass and not a mixed
decision_order: no records at all for this SHA, under either kind: no_evidence
every group verdict in action_success.success_statuses: success
no group verdict in action_success.success_statuses: failed
action_success.detail: action_detail lists one entry per group: kind, workflow, task, category, status, run_id, and whether that verdict is what drove the row state
action_success.category_grouping: category is the classification that caused the evidence (ADR-0002 section 2.2) and is what tells the UI which column's workflow failed; in v1 it equals kind, and the grouping is therefore kind-shaped today and forward-compatible tomorrow
action_success.no_evidence_is_not_failure: a commit with no records may never have run at all: render unknown, never failed, never ✗, never 0 %
indistinguishable_cases: no workflow ran for this SHA
a run was cancelled before publishing (ADR-0002 section 1.1: cancel publishes nothing)
a run succeeded and its extractor found nothing (meta.json evidence[] would say so, and the index may not read it)
action_success.unreadable_records_are: a SHA whose records exist but cannot be read stays no_evidence and carries unreadable_records with a count: 'unreadable' and 'never ran' are different answers, both unknown, neither a failure
action_success.resolution: mact-by1.18 (evidence contract v2: a durable run-outcome record) is what would separate these; until then the row says no_evidence and doctor may, as advisory, name a run directory that published nothing

meta_json_policy.advisory_marking: anything derived from runs/ is labelled advisory in the output and is never written into a row's contract fields
meta_json_policy.missing_or_renamed_meta_never_breaks: a render or an index run MUST NOT fail because runs/ is absent, unreadable, or has no meta.json for a run_id an evidence file names
meta_json_policy.why_not_the_index: runs/ is not commit-keyed, so joining it to a commit is a scan of every run directory; and ADR-0002 section 1.3 already says it is audit material

rules: every number carries an explicit unknown / zero / empty state; 0 always means a measured zero
unknown is the same glyph in every column, so absence never reads as a failure and a failure never reads as absence
the caveat marker is appended to the column it qualifies and the caveat codes live on the row; a marker with nothing behind it is a bug
no colour-only signal: the glyph alone must carry the state (NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb are supported terminals)
delta arrows need both sides: no parent value means no arrow, and an arrow is never a directionless decoration
--plain and fathom report --format tsv use the ascii column of this table, so a log file is readable without a unicode terminal

parent_rules.root_commit: a commit with no parent has no delta anywhere: delta fields are absent, not 0, not the value itself; absolute values still render
parent_rules.merge_commit: deltas are against the FIRST parent, which is the line history was merged onto; the evidence is whatever ran on this SHA and nothing else
parent_rules.no_inheritance: a commit never borrows a parent's or a sibling's number: no carry-forward for coverage or benchmarks, because a number attributed to a commit that never ran is a lie
parent_rules.octopus_merge: additional parents are displayable in the detail view and are never a delta base
parent_rules.config: history.first_parent (ADR-0006 section 7.2) narrows the walk; it does not change which parent a delta is against

adr_pins.$comment: the exact lines docs/adr/0008 section 0 duplicates; C2 requires the ADR block to equal this object field for field, and each value to agree with the normative field it names
adr_pins.percent_input: raw counts only, never a rounded intermediate
adr_pins.coverage_pool: sum of numerators over sum of denominators, per measure
adr_pins.vacuous_found_zero: no number, reason vacuous, excluded from every average
adr_pins.benchmark_value: median over the samples of the newest selected run
adr_pins.median_even_n: mean of the two middle values
adr_pins.benchmark_spread: min and max over every retained run of that group
adr_pins.action_source: the run_status field on every evidence record

forbidden: average per-file or per-run percentages instead of summing numerators and denominators
use sum(file records) == total as a validity check
plot or diff a percent_only or low_confidence record
compare, diff or plot values whose unit differs or is absent
treat an absent value as 0, as an empty string, or as a regression
read runs/ or incoming/ in the index path
join evidence on a short SHA
carry a parent's number forward to a child with no evidence
sum the surviving records of a truncated run and call it the run
invent a denominator for a scraped percentage
silently prefer one of two disagreeing coverage sources
average across commits, per-file, or per-run to fill a hole in a history sparkline
